docs.title: Welcome to Bioctree
docs.text:
Spatiotemporal–Spectral Signal Processing on Cortical Manifolds

A comprehensive MATLAB toolbox for analyzing neural signals on brain surface meshes using graph signal processing and spectral geometry.

docs.title: Core Features
docs.text:
• Wave Packet Analysis

    Detect and characterize traveling waves on cortical surfaces with precise spatiotemporal-spectral localization.

    Learn about wave packets

  • Spectral Filtering

    Design and apply filters in eigenspace with guaranteed spatial localization properties using Laplace–Beltrami operators.

    Explore filters

  • Joint Domain Processing

    Unified framework for signals on product spaces: spatial × temporal, spatial × spectral, and beyond.

    Joint domains

  • Manifold-Based Analysis

    Finite element methods (FEM) and differential geometry for cortical mesh processing.

    Manifold concepts

  • HDF5-Based Storage

    Efficient .bct file format for storing mesh data, eigenbases, signals, and comprehensive metadata.

    File format spec

  • Graph Signal Processing

    Leverage GSP tools and techniques adapted for cortical surface analysis with spectral graph theory.

    Graph structure

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Get up and running in minutes with Bioctree:

% Load a cortical mesh
data = load('data/mesh/fsaverage_rh_pial.mat');
B = bct.bct.fromMesh(data.V, data.F);

% Compute Laplace–Beltrami eigenbasis
B = B.computeEigenbasis(256);

% Create a signal and filter it
signal = B.createSignal(data);
filtered = signal.lowpass(cutoff_freq);

Full Quickstart Guide

docs.title: Neural Signal Processing Meets Differential Geometry
docs.text:
Bioctree bridges computational neuroscience and differential geometry by providing:

  • Laplace–Beltrami eigenbasis computation for arbitrary cortical meshes
  • Wave packet transforms with joint time-frequency-space localization
  • Dispersion analysis for characterizing wave propagation dynamics
  • Spatiotemporal filtering using tensor product operators

docs.title: Example: Detecting Traveling Waves
docs.text:
Identify and characterize neural traveling waves on cortical surfaces:

% Detect wave packets in spatiotemporal data
params = struct(...
    'f_min', 8, ...
    'f_max', 12, ...
    'detection_threshold', 2.5 ...
);

[detections, wt_coeffs] = bct.sim.detectWavePackets(signal, params);

% Visualize wave trajectories on the cortical mesh
bct.show.waveTrajectories(detections, B.manifold);

% Load and initialize
data = load('mesh.mat');

docs.title: BCT File Specification
docs.text: The BCT (Bioctree) file format is an HDF5-based standard for storing neuroimaging data with mesh geometry, signals, and metadata.

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
dataset_name.h5
├── /raw/                      % Raw signals
│   ├── X                      % Signal data [N × T] or [L × T × N]
│   ├── fs                     % Sampling frequency (Hz)
│   └── layer_ids              % Layer identifiers (if multi-layer)
├── /graph/                    % Mesh/graph structure
│   ├── V                      % Vertices [N × 3]
│   ├── F                      % Faces [M × 3]
│   └── edges                  % Edge list [E × 2]
├── /tf/                       % Time-frequency coefficients (optional)
│   ├── coeffs_real            % Real part [L × F × T × N]
│   ├── coeffs_imag            % Imaginary part [L × F × T × N]
│   ├── freqs                  % Frequency vector [F × 1]
│   └── params/                % Transform parameters
└── /metadata/                 % Metadata
    ├── schema_version         % BCT schema version
    ├── created                % Timestamp
    └── description            % Text description

docs.title: Creating BCT Files
docs.text:
% Create new file
bct_obj = bct.create('my_dataset');

% Write signal data
bct_obj.write_raw(signal_matrix, sampling_rate);

% Write mesh
graph_struct = struct('V', vertices, 'F', faces);
bct_obj.write_graph(graph_struct);

% Validate
report = bct_obj.validate();

docs.title: Reading BCT Files
docs.text:
% Open existing file
bct_obj = bct.open('my_dataset.h5');

% Read full data
data = bct_obj.read_raw();

% Read partial (time range 100-500, vertices 1-1000)
subset = bct_obj.read_raw([100, 500], [1, 1000]);

% Read graph
graph = bct_obj.read_graph();

docs.title: Multi-Layer Support
docs.text:
% Stack multiple conditions/trials as layers
layer_1 = condition_A_data;  % [N × T]
layer_2 = condition_B_data;  % [N × T]

% Combine into 3D array [L × T × N]
multi_layer = cat(1, ...
    reshape(layer_1, [1, size(layer_1)]), ...
    reshape(layer_2, [1, size(layer_2)]));

% Write
bct_obj.write_raw_layers(multi_layer, fs, [0, 1]);

% Read specific layer
layer_1_read = bct_obj.read_raw_layers(1, ':', ':');

docs.title: Schema Validation
docs.text:
% Validate against schema
report = bct_obj.validate();

if report.ok
    fprintf('✓ File is valid\n');
else
    fprintf('Validation errors:\n');
    fprintf('%s\n', report.messages{:});
end

docs.title: fromMesh
docs.text:
Create from mesh vertices and faces: 

B = bct.bct.fromMesh(V, F);

Parameters: - V: [N × 3] vertex coordinates - F: [M × 3] face indices (1-based)

docs.title: fromGraph
docs.text:
Create from graph adjacency: 

B = bct.bct.fromGraph(W);

Parameters: - W: [N × N] sparse adjacency/weight matrix

docs.title: Manifold
docs.text:
Geometric structure (mesh or graph). 

M = B.Manifold;  % bct.Manifold object

docs.title: Lambda
docs.text:
Spectral domain (eigenmode space). 

Lambda = B.Lambda;  % bct.Lambda object (if computed)

docs.title: Time
docs.text:
Temporal dimension. 

T = B.Time;  % bct.Time object (if set)

docs.title: Omega
docs.text:
Frequency domain. 

Omega = B.Omega;  % bct.Omega object (if Time is set)

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
Array of signals. 

sigs = B.Signals;  % Array of bct.Signal objects

docs.title: computeEigenbasis
docs.text:
Compute eigenmodes of Laplace-Beltrami operator.

Syntax: 

B.computeEigenbasis(K);
B.computeEigenbasis(K, Name, Value);

Parameters: - K: Number of eigenmodes to compute

Name-Value Pairs: - 'Method': 'sparse' (default) or 'dense' - 'Tolerance': Eigenvalue tolerance (default: 1e-6) - 'UseGPU': Use GPU acceleration (default: false)

Example: 

B.computeEigenbasis(100);
B.computeEigenbasis(100, 'Method', 'sparse', 'Tolerance', 1e-8);

docs.title: addSignal
docs.text:
Add signal to collection.

Syntax: 

B.addSignal(signal);

Parameters: - signal: bct.Signal object

Example: 

sig = bct.Signal(B.Manifold, data, 'my_signal');
B.addSignal(sig);

docs.title: removeSignal
docs.text:
Remove signal from collection.

Syntax: 

B.removeSignal(index_or_label);

Example: 

B.removeSignal(1);            % Remove first signal
B.removeSignal('my_signal');  % Remove by label

docs.title: getSignalByLabel
docs.text:
Retrieve signal by label.

Syntax: 

sig = B.getSignalByLabel(label);

Returns: bct.Signal object or empty if not found

docs.title: getJointDomain
docs.text:
Create tensor product domain.

Syntax: 

joint = B.getJointDomain(domain1_name, domain2_name);

Example: 

lambda_omega = B.getJointDomain('Lambda', 'Omega');

docs.title: computeDispersion
docs.text:
Estimate dispersion relation from data.

Syntax: 

B.computeDispersion(signal);
B.computeDispersion(signal, Name, Value);

Name-Value Pairs: - 'Type': 'linear', 'sqrt', 'polynomial' - 'Order': Polynomial order (if Type=’polynomial’)

docs.title: Complete Workflow
docs.text:
% Create from mesh
B = bct.bct.fromMesh(V, F);

% Compute eigenbasis
B.computeEigenbasis(100);

% Add temporal dimension
B.Manifold.Time = bct.Time(200, 250);

% Create signal
data = randn(B.Manifold.N, 200);
sig = bct.Signal(B.Manifold, data, 'test');
B.addSignal(sig);

% Create filter
filt = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'lowpass', 'cutoff', 30);

% Apply
filtered = filt.apply(sig);

% Visualize
bct.show.signal(B, filtered);

docs.title: Filter API Reference
docs.text: The bct.Filter class provides filtering operations on any domain.

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
filt = bct.Filter(domain, kernel_type, Name, Value, ...);

Parameters: - domain: Domain where filter operates (Manifold, Lambda, Time, Omega, Joint) - kernel_type: String specifying kernel (see Kernel Types below) - Name, Value: Kernel-specific parameters

docs.title: ‘gaussian’
docs.text:
filt = bct.Filter(domain, 'gaussian', ...
    'center', center_value, ...
    'sigma', bandwidth);

docs.title: ‘lowpass’
docs.text: filt = bct.Filter(domain, 'lowpass', 'cutoff', cutoff_value);

docs.title: ‘highpass’
docs.text: filt = bct.Filter(domain, 'highpass', 'cutoff', cutoff_value);

docs.title: ‘bandpass’
docs.text:
filt = bct.Filter(domain, 'bandpass', ...
    'low', low_cutoff, ...
    'high', high_cutoff, ...
    'taper', true);  % Optional smooth transitions

docs.title: ‘notch’
docs.text:
filt = bct.Filter(domain, 'notch', ...
    'center', center_value, ...
    'width', notch_width);

docs.title: ‘delta’
docs.text: filt = bct.Filter(domain, 'delta', 'x0', location);

docs.title: ‘separable’ (Joint domains only)
docs.text:
filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'separable', ...
    'spatial', spatial_filter, ...
    'temporal', temporal_filter);

docs.title: ‘wavepacket’
docs.text:
filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'wavepacket', ...
    'velocity', group_velocity, ...
    'center_freq', center_frequency, ...
    'bandwidth', freq_bandwidth);

docs.title: ‘custom’
docs.text: filt = bct.Filter(domain, 'custom', 'kernel', kernel_values);

docs.title: apply
docs.text:
Apply filter to signal.

filtered_signal = filt.apply(original_signal);

Parameters: - original_signal: bct.Signal object

Returns: bct.Signal object (filtered)

docs.title: evaluate
docs.text:
Get kernel values.

kernel = filt.evaluate();

Returns: Array of filter weights

docs.title: plot
docs.text:
Visualize filter kernel.

filt.plot();
filt.plot(Name, Value);

docs.title: Spatial Smoothing
docs.text:
spatial_filt = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'gaussian', ...
    'center', 0, 'sigma', 20);
smoothed = spatial_filt.apply(signal);

docs.title: Temporal Band-Pass
docs.text:
alpha_filt = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'bandpass', ...
    'low', 8, 'high', 12, 'taper', true);
alpha = alpha_filt.apply(signal);

docs.title: Joint Filtering
docs.text:
joint = bct.Joint(B.Lambda, B.Omega);
joint_filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'gaussian', ...
    'center', [20, 10], 'sigma', [5, 2]);
result = joint_filt.apply(signal);

docs.title: Chain Filters
docs.text:
% Apply multiple filters sequentially
sig1 = filter1.apply(signal);
sig2 = filter2.apply(sig1);
sig3 = filter3.apply(sig2);

docs.title: Performance Tips
docs.text:
1. Use separable filters for joint domains when possible
  2. Evaluate kernel once if applying to multiple signals
  3. Prefer spectral domain for spatial filtering (faster)

docs.text: The bct.Joint class represents tensor products of domains.

docs.title: Constructor

Dimensions: [K × F] where K = num eigenmodes, F = num frequencies

docs.title: Time × Lambda

joint_time_spectral = bct.Joint(B.Time, B.Lambda);

docs.title: Higher-Order
docs.text:
% Lambda × Omega × Layer
joint_3d = bct.Joint(B.Lambda, B.Omega, Layer);

docs.title: Manifold Class Reference
docs.text: The bct.Manifold class represents geometric meshes or graphs.

docs.title: From Vertices and Faces
docs.text:
M = bct.Manifold(V, F);

Parameters: - V: [N × 3] vertex coordinates in ℝ³ - F: [M × 3] face indices (1-based)

docs.title: From Graph
docs.text:
M = bct.Manifold.fromGraph(W);

Parameters: - W: [N × N] sparse adjacency/weight matrix

docs.title: V
docs.text:
Vertex positions. 

V = M.V;  % [N × 3] double

docs.title: F
docs.text:
Face connectivity. 

F = M.F;  % [M × 3] int32

docs.title: N
docs.text:
Number of vertices (dependent property). 

num_vertices = M.N;

docs.title: Type
docs.text:
Manifold type (dependent property). 

type = M.Type;  % 'mesh' or 'graph'

docs.title: Edges
docs.text:
Edge list (computed from faces or adjacency). 

E = M.Edges;  % [E × 2] int32

docs.title: Time
docs.text:
Optional temporal dimension. 

M.Time = bct.Time(200, 250);  % 200 samples at 250 Hz

docs.title: cotLaplacian
docs.text:
Compute cotangent Laplacian matrix.

L = M.cotLaplacian();  % [N × N] sparse

Returns: Symmetric sparse Laplace-Beltrami matrix

docs.text:
Compute mass matrix (vertex areas).

Mass = M.massMatrix();  % [N × N] sparse diagonal

docs.title: plot

M.plot();
M.plot(Name, Value);

Name-Value Pairs: - 'FaceColor': Color specification - 'EdgeColor': Edge color - 'FaceAlpha': Transparency (0-1)

distances = M.geodesicDistance(source_vertex);

grad = M.computeGradient(scalar_field);  % [N × 3]

docs.title: bct.bct
docs.text:
Main orchestrator for all operations.

Constructor: 

B = bct.bct.fromMesh(V, F);
B = bct.bct.fromGraph(W);

Key Methods: - computeEigenbasis(K) - Compute K eigenmodes - addSignal(signal) - Add signal to collection - getJointDomain(d1, d2) - Create tensor product domain

Properties: - Manifold - Geometry - Lambda - Spectral domain - Time - Temporal domain (if set) - Omega - Frequency domain (if set) - Signals - Signal array

docs.title: bct.Domain (Abstract)
docs.text:
Base class for all domains.

Required Methods (must implement in subclasses): - size() - Dimension of domain - axes() - Coordinate axes - dual() - Dual domain

docs.title: bct.Manifold
docs.text:
Geometric mesh or graph.

Constructor: 

M = bct.Manifold(V, F);            % From vertices and faces
M = bct.Manifold.fromGraph(W);     % From adjacency matrix

Properties: - V - Vertices [N × 3] - F - Faces [M × 3] - N - Number of vertices - Edges - Edge list - Time - Temporal dimension (optional)

Methods: - cotLaplacian() - Compute Laplace-Beltrami matrix - massMatrix() - Compute mass matrix - plot() - Visualize mesh - transform(signal, target_domain) - Transform signal

docs.title: bct.Lambda
docs.text:
Spectral domain (eigenmode space).

Constructor: 

Lambda = bct.Lambda.fromManifold(M, num_modes);

Properties: - eigenvalues - Spatial frequencies [K × 1] - eigenvectors - Eigenmodes [N × K] - K - Number of modes

Methods: - forward(signal) - Manifold → Lambda transform - inverse(coeffs) - Lambda → Manifold transform - plotDispersion() - Visualize dispersion relation

docs.title: bct.Signal
docs.text:
Signals defined on domains.

Constructor: 

sig = bct.Signal(domain, data, label);

Properties: - Data - Signal values - Domain - Domain where signal lives - Label - String identifier

Dependent Properties: - IsStatic - True if no time dimension - IsDynamic - True if has time dimension - IsVector - True if vector-valued

filt = bct.Filter(domain, kernel_type, param1, value1, ...);

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Dispersion describes how waves of different frequencies propagate at different speeds on a manifold. Understanding dispersion is crucial for detecting and characterizing traveling waves in cortical signals.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
The relationship between temporal frequency \(\omega\) and spatial frequency \(\lambda\):

\[ \omega = \omega(\lambda) \]

docs.title: Physical Interpretation
docs.text:
• Non-dispersive (\(\omega \propto \lambda\)): All frequencies travel at same speed
  • Dispersive (\(\omega \propto f(\lambda)\) nonlinear): Different frequencies spread out over time

docs.title: 1. Linear (Non-Dispersive)
docs.text:
\[\omega = c \lambda\]

where \(c\) is constant velocity.

Example: Diffusion on flat surfaces

% Linear dispersion
c = 0.5;  % m/s
omega = c * lambda;

docs.title: 2. Square Root (Weakly Dispersive)
3. General Polynomial
From Data
docs.text:
% Load spatiotemporal signal
signal = bct.Signal(B.Manifold, data_NxT, 'meg_data');

% Compute dispersion relation
B.computeDispersion(signal);

% Access fitted parameters
omega_of_lambda = B.Lambda.dispersion;
dispersion_type = B.Lambda.dispersionType;
coefficients = B.Lambda.dispersionCoeffs;

docs.title: Visualization
docs.text:
% Plot dispersion relation
figure;
B.Lambda.plotDispersion();
xlabel('Spatial Frequency λ (eigenvalue)');
ylabel('Temporal Frequency ω (Hz)');
title('Dispersion Relation');
grid on;

docs.title: Phase Velocity
docs.text:
Speed of phase fronts:

\[ v_p(\lambda) = \frac{\omega(\lambda)}{\lambda} \] 
% Compute phase velocity
vp = B.Lambda.phaseVelocity();

% Plot
plot(B.Lambda.eigenvalues, vp);
xlabel('λ');
ylabel('v_p (m/s)');
title('Phase Velocity');

docs.title: Group Velocity
docs.text:
Speed of wave packet envelope:

\[ v_g(\lambda) = \frac{d\omega(\lambda)}{d\lambda} \] 
% Compute group velocity
vg = B.Lambda.groupVelocity();

% Plot both
figure;
plot(B.Lambda.eigenvalues, vp, 'DisplayName', 'Phase');
hold on;
plot(B.Lambda.eigenvalues, vg, 'DisplayName', 'Group');
legend;
xlabel('λ');
ylabel('Velocity (m/s)');

docs.title: Filter for Specific Velocity
docs.text:
% Extract waves traveling at 0.5 m/s
vg_filter = bct.Filter(joint, 'groupvelocity', ...
    'target', 0.5, ...         % Target velocity
    'tolerance', 0.1);         % ±0.1 m/s

waves_05 = vg_filter.apply(signal);

docs.title: Multi-Velocity Decomposition
docs.text:
% Decompose into velocity components
velocities = [0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.2];  % m/s

for i = 1:length(velocities)
    filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'groupvelocity', ...
        'target', velocities(i), 'tolerance', 0.1);

    components{i} = filt.apply(signal);
end

docs.title: Measure from Cross-Spectrum
docs.text:
% Compute cross-spectrum between spatial modes
cross_spec = B.Lambda.crossSpectrum(signal);

% Extract peak frequencies per mode
[peak_freqs, peak_powers] = B.Lambda.peakFrequencies(cross_spec);

% Fit dispersion relation
[coeffs, fit_quality] = B.Lambda.fitDispersion(peak_freqs);

docs.title: Validate Dispersion Model
docs.text:
% Compute residuals
omega_predicted = B.Lambda.dispersion(lambda_values);
omega_measured = measured_frequencies;
residuals = omega_measured - omega_predicted;

% R² goodness of fit
R2 = 1 - sum(residuals.^2) / sum((omega_measured - mean(omega_measured)).^2);
fprintf('R² = %.3f\n', R2);

docs.title: Dispersion-Aware Wave Packets
docs.text:
% Use empirical dispersion relation
wp_filter = bct.Filter(joint, 'wavepacket', ...
    'dispersion', B.Lambda.dispersion, ...  % Use fitted relation
    'center_freq', 10, ...
    'bandwidth', 2);

wp_signal = wp_filter.apply(signal);

docs.title: Chirp Detection
docs.text:
For dispersive media, wave packets “chirp” (change frequency):

% Detect chirping wave packets
chirp_filter = bct.Filter(joint, 'chirp', ...
    'dispersion', B.Lambda.dispersion, ...
    'start_freq', 8, ...
    'end_freq', 12, ...
    'duration', 0.5);  % seconds

docs.title: 1. Differentiate Wave Types
docs.text:
% Alpha waves (linear dispersion)
alpha_disp = B.computeDispersion(alpha_signal, 'Type', 'linear');

% Spindles (dispersive)
spindle_disp = B.computeDispersion(spindle_signal, 'Type', 'sqrt');

% Compare
figure;
subplot(1,2,1); alpha_disp.plot(); title('Alpha');
subplot(1,2,2); spindle_disp.plot(); title('Spindles');

docs.title: 2. Wave Speed Mapping
docs.text:
% Create velocity map across cortex
vg_map = zeros(B.Manifold.N, 1);
for i = 1:B.Manifold.N
    % Dominant frequency at vertex i
    [~, dom_freq_idx] = max(abs(fft(signal.Data(i, :))));
    dom_lambda = B.Lambda.eigenvalues(dom_freq_idx);

    % Group velocity at that frequency
    vg_map(i) = B.Lambda.groupVelocity(dom_lambda);
end

% Visualize
bct.show.signal(B, vg_map, 'Title', 'Group Velocity Map');

docs.title: 3. Direction-Resolved Waves
docs.text:
% Combine velocity with direction
phase_grad = B.Manifold.computeGradient(phase);
wave_velocity_vectors = vg_map .* phase_grad;

% Show as vector field
bct.show.vectorField(B, wave_velocity_vectors);

docs.title: Fitting Algorithms
docs.text:
% Least squares (default)
B.computeDispersion('Method', 'leastsquares');

% Robust fit (outlier resistant)
B.computeDispersion('Method', 'robust');

% Weighted fit (confidence weights)
B.computeDispersion('Method', 'weighted', 'Weights', weights);

docs.title: Uncertainty Quantification
docs.text:
% Bootstrap confidence intervals
[coeffs, ci] = B.computeDispersion('Bootstrap', true, 'Iterations', 1000);

% Plot with confidence bands
B.Lambda.plotDispersion('ConfidenceIntervals', true);

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Graphs generalize signal processing from regular grids to irregular network structures. In Bioctree, graphs are treated as abstract manifolds where connectivity matters more than geometric embedding.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: A graph \(\mathcal{G} = (V, E, W)\) consists of: - Vertices \(V = \{1, 2, \ldots, N\}\) - Edges \(E \subseteq V \times V\) - Weights \(W: E \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^+\) (optional)

docs.title: Adjacency Matrix
docs.text: \[ W_{ij} = \begin{cases} w_{ij} & \text{if } (i,j) \in E \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

docs.title: Edge List
docs.text:
edges = [
    1, 2, 0.5;   % vertex 1 connected to 2, weight 0.5
    1, 3, 0.3;
    2, 3, 0.8;
    ...
];

docs.title: Unnormalized Laplacian
docs.text:
\[ L = D - W \]

where \(D\) is the degree matrix: \(D_{ii} = \sum_j W_{ij}\)

Properties: - Symmetric, positive semi-definite - \(L \mathbf{1} = 0\) (constant is in kernel) - Smallest eigenvalue is 0

docs.title: Normalized Laplacian
docs.text:
\[ \mathcal{L} = D^{-1/2} L D^{-1/2} = I - D^{-1/2} W D^{-1/2} \]

Advantage: Eigenvalues in \([0, 2]\), better for heterogeneous graphs

docs.title: Bioctree Usage
docs.text:
% Create from adjacency matrix
W = sparse(adjacency_matrix);
G = bct.Graph(W);

% Access Laplacian
L = G.laplacian();            % Unnormalized
L_norm = G.laplacian('normalized');

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
For signal \(f\) on graph vertices:

Forward: \(\(\hat{f} = U^T f\)\)

Inverse: \(\(f = U \hat{f}\)\)

where \(U\) contains eigenvectors of \(L\): \(LU = U\Lambda\)

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text:
• Eigenvectors \(u_i\): Graph Fourier bases
  • Eigenvalues \(\lambda_i\): Graph frequencies
  • Coefficients \(\hat{f}_i\): Frequency content
% Compute graph eigenbasis
B = bct.bct.fromGraph(W);
B.computeEigenbasis(50);

% Transform signal
f_hat = B.Lambda.forward(f);  % To frequency domain
f_reconstructed = B.Lambda.inverse(f_hat);

docs.title: Graph vs. Mesh
docs.text: Aspect Graph Mesh Geometry Abstract Embedded in ℝ³ Edges Arbitrary From triangulation Weights Custom Cotangent formula Curvature N/A Defined Visualization Network layout 3D surface

docs.title: When to Use Each
docs.text:
Use Graph: - Social networks - Sensor networks - Abstract connectivity (e.g., functional brain networks) - Custom edge weights (correlations, distances, etc.)

Use Mesh: - Cortical surfaces - 3D shapes - Geometric data with spatial embedding - When curvature and geometry matter

docs.title: Creating Graphs
docs.text:
% From adjacency matrix
W = sparse(N, N);
W(i, j) = weight;  % Add edges
B = bct.bct.fromGraph(W);

% From edge list
edges = [source, target, weight];
B = bct.bct.fromEdgeList(edges);

% From mesh (convert to graph)
M = bct.Manifold(V, F);
G = M.toGraph();

docs.title: Graph Filtering
docs.text:
% Low-pass filter (smooth on graph)
filt = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'lowpass', 'cutoff', 10);
f_smooth = filt.apply(f);

% High-pass (detect irregular patterns)
filt_hp = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'highpass', 'cutoff', 20);
f_edges = filt_hp.apply(f);

docs.title: Spectral Clustering
docs.text:
% Use eigenvectors for clustering
k = 5;  % Number of clusters
features = B.Lambda.eigenvectors(:, 2:k+1);  % Skip DC
clusters = kmeans(features, k);

% Visualize clusters
scatter3(features(:,1), features(:,2), features(:,3), 20, clusters, 'filled');

docs.title: Graph Wavelets
docs.text:
% Create wavelet filter bank
scales = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16];
wavelets = bct.filters.graphWavelets(B.Lambda, scales);

% Apply wavelets
coeffs = cell(length(scales), 1);
for i = 1:length(scales)
    coeffs{i} = wavelets{i}.apply(signal);
end

docs.title: Diffusion
docs.text:
% Heat diffusion on graph
t = 1.0;  % Time
f_diffused = B.Lambda.diffuse(f_initial, t);

docs.title: Random Walks
docs.text:
% Transition matrix
P = G.transitionMatrix();

% k-step random walk
k = 10;
distribution = P^k * initial_distribution;

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: The Joint Domain in Bioctree represents the tensor product of multiple 1D domains, enabling multidimensional spectral analysis. The most common is the joint spectral-temporal domain: Lambda × Omega.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
Many real-world signals have structure in multiple dimensions simultaneously:

  • Neural oscillations: Specific spatial patterns at specific frequencies
  • Traveling waves: Coupled spatiotemporal dynamics
  • Event-related responses: Transient spatiotemporal patterns

Standard separated analysis (spatial-then-temporal) misses joint structure.

docs.title: Tensor Product of Domains
docs.text:
For domains \(\mathcal{D}_1\) and \(\mathcal{D}_2\):

\[ \mathcal{D}_1 \otimes \mathcal{D}_2 = \{(x_1, x_2) : x_1 \in \mathcal{D}_1, x_2 \in \mathcal{D}_2\} \]

docs.title: Joint Transform
docs.text:
Forward transform (2D): $$ \hat{f}(i, j) = \langle f, \phi_i \otimes \psi_j \rangle $$

where \(\phi_i\) are bases of \(\mathcal{D}_1\) and \(\psi_j\) are bases of \(\mathcal{D}_2\).

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
\[ \text{Joint} = \Lambda \otimes \Omega \]
  • Lambda: Spatial frequency (eigenmodes)
  • Omega: Temporal frequency (Hz)

Dimensions: \([K \times F]\) where: - \(K\): Number of eigenmodes - \(F\): Number of frequency bins

docs.title: Creating Joint Domains
docs.text:
% Create BCT object with eigenbasis
B = bct.bct.fromMesh(V, F);
B.computeEigenbasis(100);

% Add temporal dimension
B.Manifold.Time = bct.Time(200, 250);  % 200 samples at 250 Hz

% Joint domain is automatically available
joint = bct.Joint(B.Lambda, B.Omega);

% Or access via BCT object
joint = B.getJointDomain('Lambda', 'Omega');

docs.title: Separable Filters
docs.text:
Product of 1D filters: $$ h(i, j) = h_{\Lambda}(i) \cdot h_{\Omega}(j) $$

% Spatial low-pass × Temporal band-pass
spatial_filt = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'lowpass', 'cutoff', 30);
temporal_filt = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'bandpass', 'low', 8, 'high', 12);

% Combined separable filter
joint_filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'separable', ...
    'spatial', spatial_filt, ...
    'temporal', temporal_filt);

docs.title: Non-Separable Filters
docs.text:
General 2D kernel \(h(i, j)\) that cannot be factored:

% 2D Gaussian on joint domain
joint_filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'gaussian', ...
    'center', [20, 10], ...   % [spatial_mode, freq_Hz]
    'sigma', [5, 2]);         % [spatial_bw, freq_bw]

% Apply to spatiotemporal signal
sig = bct.Signal(B.Manifold, data_NxT, 'meg_data');
filtered = joint_filt.apply(sig);

docs.title: 1. Oscillation Detection
docs.text:
Find spatial patterns oscillating at specific frequencies:

% Alpha oscillation (8-12 Hz) with smooth spatial pattern
alpha_filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'gaussian', ...
    'center', [10, 10], ...   % Low spatial freq, 10 Hz temporal
    'sigma', [5, 2]);

alpha_pattern = alpha_filt.apply(signal);

docs.title: 2. Traveling Wave Analysis
docs.text:
% Wave with specific velocity
% Uses dispersion relation: ω = c|λ|
wave_filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'wavepacket', ...
    'velocity', 0.5, ...      % m/s
    'center_freq', 10, ...    % Hz
    'bandwidth', 2);

wave_signal = wave_filt.apply(signal);

docs.title: 3. Multi-Scale Time-Frequency
docs.text:
% Different spatial scales at different frequencies
bands = [
    1, 20, 4, 8;      % Spatial 1-20, Temporal 4-8 Hz
    20, 40, 8, 12;    % Spatial 20-40, Temporal 8-12 Hz
    40, 60, 13, 30;   % Spatial 40-60, Temporal 13-30 Hz
];

for i = 1:size(bands, 1)
    filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'bandpass', ...
        'spatial_low', bands(i,1), 'spatial_high', bands(i,2), ...
        'temporal_low', bands(i,3), 'temporal_high', bands(i,4));

    decomposition{i} = filt.apply(signal);
end

docs.title: 2D Spectrum
docs.text:
% Compute joint spectrum
spectrum_2d = joint.computeSpectrum(signal);

% Visualize as heatmap
figure;
imagesc(spectrum_2d);
xlabel('Temporal Frequency (Hz)');
ylabel('Spatial Frequency (Eigenmode)');
colorbar;
title('Joint Spectral-Temporal Power');

docs.title: Filter Kernel Visualization
docs.text:
% Visualize 2D filter kernel
filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'gaussian', ...);
kernel_2d = filt.evaluate();

figure;
imagesc(kernel_2d);
xlabel('Omega (Hz)');
ylabel('Lambda (Mode)');
title('Joint Filter Kernel');
colorbar;

docs.title: 3D: Lambda × Omega × Layer
docs.text:
For multi-condition experiments:

% Add layer dimension
Layer = bct.Layer([1, 2, 3]);  % 3 experimental conditions

% Create 3D joint domain
joint_3d = bct.Joint(B.Lambda, B.Omega, Layer);

% 3D filter
filt_3d = bct.Filter(joint_3d, 'gaussian', ...
    'center', [20, 10, 2], ...  % [spatial, temporal, layer]
    'sigma', [5, 2, 0.5]);

docs.title: Time × Lambda (Time-Varying Spatial)
docs.text:
% Joint time-spectral (different from Lambda × Omega!)
joint_time_lambda = bct.Joint(B.Time, B.Lambda);

% Filter: smooth in time, bandpass in space
filt = bct.Filter(joint_time_lambda, 'separable', ...
    'time', bct.Filter(B.Time, 'gaussian', 'sigma', 10), ...
    'lambda', bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'bandpass', 'low', 20, 'high', 40));

docs.title: Separable Kernels
docs.text:
For separable filters, use 1D operations:

% Instead of 2D convolution
% Step 1: Filter in spatial domain
sig_spatial = spatial_filt.apply(signal);

% Step 2: Filter in temporal domain
sig_both = temporal_filt.apply(sig_spatial);

% Result same as joint filter, but faster

% Keep other dimension in time/space
sig_spectral = B.Lambda.forward(signal);  % [K × T]

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: The Laplace-Beltrami operator is the generalization of the Laplacian to curved manifolds. It is the foundation for spectral analysis on surfaces in Bioctree.

docs.title: In 1D (Line)
docs.text: The second derivative measures curvature: \(\(\frac{d^2 f}{dx^2}\)\)

docs.title: In 2D Euclidean (Plane)
docs.text: The Laplacian: \(\(\Delta f = \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2} + \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial y^2}\)\)

docs.title: On Manifolds (Curved Surfaces)
docs.text: The Laplace-Beltrami operator \(\Delta_{\mathcal{M}}\) extends this to arbitrary surfaces, accounting for curvature.

docs.title: Continuous Form
docs.text:
On a smooth manifold \(\mathcal{M}\) with metric \(g\):

\[ \Delta_{\mathcal{M}} f = \frac{1}{\sqrt{|g|}} \partial_i \left(\sqrt{|g|} g^{ij} \partial_j f\right) \]

Physical interpretation: Measures how much a function differs from its local average.

docs.title: Discrete Form (Cotangent Laplacian)
docs.text:
For triangle meshes, the discrete Laplace-Beltrami matrix is:

\[ L_{ij} = \begin{cases} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{N}(i)} w_{ik} & \text{if } i = j \\ -w_{ij} & \text{if } j \in \mathcal{N}(i) \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

where the weights are:

\[ w_{ij} = \frac{1}{2}(\cot \alpha_{ij} + \cot \beta_{ij}) \]

\(\alpha_{ij}\) and \(\beta_{ij}\) are angles opposite edge \((i,j)\) in adjacent triangles.

docs.title: The Eigenvalue Problem
docs.text:
\[ L \phi_i = \lambda_i M \phi_i \]

where: - \(L\): Laplacian matrix [N × N] - \(M\): Mass matrix [N × N] (diagonal) - \(\lambda_i\): Eigenvalues (spatial frequencies) - \(\phi_i\): Eigenvectors (spatial modes)

docs.title: Properties of Eigenmodes
docs.text:
1. Orthogonality: \(\(\phi_i^T M \phi_j = \delta_{ij}\)\)

  2. Completeness: Any function can be represented: \(\(f = \sum_{i=1}^{N} \hat{f}_i \phi_i\)\)

  3. Ordering: \(0 = \lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \lambda_3 \le \cdots \le \lambda_N\)

  4. Physical meaning:

  5. \(\lambda_i\): Characteristic “frequency” of mode \(i\)
  6. Small \(\lambda_i\): Smooth, global patterns
  7. Large \(\lambda_i\): Oscillatory, local patterns

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
% Create manifold
M = bct.Manifold(V, F);

% Create BCT object
B = bct.bct.fromManifold(M);

% Compute first 100 eigenmodes
B.computeEigenbasis(100);

% Access eigenvalues and eigenvectors
lambdas = B.Lambda.eigenvalues;     % [100 × 1]
phi = B.Lambda.eigenvectors;        % [N × 100]

docs.title: Advanced Options
docs.text:
% Use sparse solver (faster for K << N)
B.computeEigenbasis(100, 'Method', 'sparse');

% Specify tolerance
B.computeEigenbasis(100, 'Tolerance', 1e-8);

% Use GPU acceleration (if available)
B.computeEigenbasis(100, 'UseGPU', true);

docs.title: Low Frequency Modes (Smooth)
docs.text:
% First 5 modes (after constant mode 0)
bct.show.eigenmodes(B, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]);

Mode 1 (\(\lambda_1 = 0\)): Constant function (DC component) Mode 2-5: Gradually increasing spatial oscillations

docs.title: High Frequency Modes (Oscillatory)
docs.text:
% High modes show rapid spatial variation
bct.show.eigenmodes(B, [95, 96, 97, 98, 99, 100]);

docs.title: Heat Equation
docs.text:
The Laplace-Beltrami operator governs heat diffusion:

\[ \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = -\Delta_{\mathcal{M}} u \]

Solution: $$ u(t) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} e^{-\lambda_i t} \hat{u}_i \phi_i $$

  • Low \(\lambda_i\) modes decay slowly (persist over time)
  • High \(\lambda_i\) modes decay rapidly (smooth out quickly)
% Simulate heat diffusion
initial_condition = zeros(N, 1);
initial_condition(100) = 1;  % Point heat source

% Diffuse over time
t = 0.1;
u_t = B.Lambda.heatDiffusion(initial_condition, t);

% Visualize
bct.show.signal(B, u_t);

docs.title: Wave Equation
docs.text:
The Laplace-Beltrami also appears in wave propagation:

\[ \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} = -c^2 \Delta_{\mathcal{M}} u \]

Eigenmodes are the natural oscillation modes of the surface.

docs.title: Forward Transform (Manifold → Lambda)
docs.text:
Project signal onto eigenbasis:

\[ \hat{f}_i = \langle f, \phi_i \rangle_M = \sum_{j=1}^{N} f_j M_{jj} \phi_{ij} \] 
% Spatial signal
f = signal_on_manifold;  % [N × 1]

% Transform to spectral domain
f_hat = B.Lambda.forward(f);  % [K × 1] coefficients

% Or using transform method
f_hat = B.Manifold.transform(f, B.Lambda);

docs.title: Inverse Transform (Lambda → Manifold)
docs.text:
Reconstruct from coefficients:

\[ f_j = \sum_{i=1}^{K} \hat{f}_i \phi_{ij} \] 
% Spectral coefficients
f_hat = spectral_coeffs;  % [K × 1]

% Inverse transform
f = B.Lambda.inverse(f_hat);  % [N × 1]

% Or using transform method
f = B.Lambda.transform(f_hat, B.Manifold);

docs.title: In the Spectral Domain
docs.text:
Filtering is multiplication in the spectral domain:

\[ \widehat{(f \ast h)} = \hat{h} \odot \hat{f} \] 
% Define filter kernel
h_lambda = zeros(100, 1);
h_lambda(1:30) = 1;  % Low-pass (keep first 30 modes)

% Filter in spectral domain
f_hat_filtered = h_lambda .* f_hat;

% Reconstruct
f_filtered = B.Lambda.inverse(f_hat_filtered);

docs.title: Using Filter Objects
docs.text:
% Create low-pass filter
filt = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'lowpass', 'cutoff', 30);

% Apply to signal (handles transforms automatically)
sig_filtered = filt.apply(sig_original);

docs.title: 1. Self-Adjoint
docs.text: \[\langle \Delta_{\mathcal{M}} f, g \rangle = \langle f, \Delta_{\mathcal{M}} g \rangle\]

docs.title: 2. Non-Positive
docs.text:
\[\langle f, \Delta_{\mathcal{M}} f \rangle \le 0\]

All eigenvalues are non-negative: \(\lambda_i \ge 0\)

docs.title: 3. Kernel
docs.text:
\[\text{ker}(\Delta_{\mathcal{M}}) = \{\text{constant functions}\}\]

The first eigenvalue is always \(\lambda_1 = 0\) with \(\phi_1 = \text{constant}\).

docs.title: 4. Spectrum
docs.text: The spectrum \(\{\lambda_i\}\) characterizes the geometry: - Shape DNA: Eigenvalues encode geometric information - Isospectral: Different shapes can have same eigenvalues (rare)

docs.title: Comparison: Euclidean vs. Manifold
docs.text: Property Euclidean \(\mathbb{R}^2\) Manifold \(\mathcal{M}\) Operator \(\Delta = \nabla^2\) \(\Delta_{\mathcal{M}}\) Basis Fourier \(e^{i\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{x}}\) Eigenmodes \(\phi_i\) Frequencies Wave numbers \(\mathbf{k}\) Eigenvalues \(\lambda_i\) Continuous Yes Discretized (mesh) Isotropy Yes Depends on geometry

docs.title: Number of Modes
docs.text:
Rule of thumb: - Exploration: \(K = N/100\) to \(N/50\) - Production: \(K = N/20\) to \(N/10\) - High fidelity: \(K = N/5\) to \(N/2\)

N = size(V, 1);
K_explore = round(N / 100);
K_production = round(N / 20);

docs.title: Sparse vs. Dense Solvers
docs.text:
% Dense (better for K > N/2)
B.computeEigenbasis(100, 'Method', 'dense');

% Sparse (better for K << N)
B.computeEigenbasis(100, 'Method', 'sparse');  % Default

docs.title: Numerical Stability
docs.text:
Issue: Ill-conditioned mass matrix Solution: Mass-lumping

% Use lumped mass matrix (diagonal approximation)
B.computeEigenbasis(100, 'MassType', 'lumped');

docs.title: 1. Spatial Smoothing
docs.text:
% Low-pass filter removes high-frequency noise
smooth_filt = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'lowpass', 'cutoff', 20);
smooth_signal = smooth_filt.apply(noisy_signal);

docs.title: 2. Edge Detection
docs.text:
% High-pass filter enhances edges
edge_filt = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'highpass', 'cutoff', 50);
edges = edge_filt.apply(signal);

docs.title: 3. Multi-Scale Decomposition
docs.text:
% Decompose into frequency bands
bands = [1, 20; 20, 40; 40, 60; 60, 80];
for i = 1:size(bands, 1)
    filt = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'bandpass', ...
        'low', bands(i,1), 'high', bands(i,2));
    band_signals{i} = filt.apply(signal);
end

docs.title: 4. Spectral Clustering
docs.text:
% Use first k eigenmodes for clustering
k = 10;
features = B.Lambda.eigenvectors(:, 1:k);
idx = kmeans(features, num_clusters);

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: A manifold in Bioctree represents the geometric substrate on which signals are defined. For neuroimaging applications, this is typically a cortical surface mesh, but the framework applies to any triangulated surface or graph.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
A discrete 2D manifold is defined by:

  1. Vertex set \(V = \{v_i\}_{i=1}^{N}\) where each \(v_i \in \mathbb{R}^3\)
  2. Face set \(F = \{f_j\}_{j=1}^{M}\) where each \(f_j\) is a triple of vertex indices

This representation is called a triangular mesh.

docs.title: Example: Cortical Surface
docs.text:
% Load fsaverage right hemisphere
data = load('data/mesh/fsaverage_rh_pial.mat');

% Vertices: [N × 3] array
V = data.V;  % 40962 × 3

% Faces: [M × 3] array of indices
F = data.F;  % 81920 × 3

% Create manifold
M = bct.Manifold(V, F);

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
M.N           % Number of vertices: 40962
M.Type        % 'mesh' or 'graph'
M.V           % Vertices [N × 3]
M.F           % Faces [M × 3]
M.Edges       % Edge list [E × 2]

docs.title: Surface Area
docs.text:
The total surface area is the sum of triangle areas:

\[ A_{total} = \sum_{j=1}^{M} A_j \]

where \(A_j\) is the area of triangle \(j\).

% Compute per-vertex areas
areas = M.computeVertexAreas();

% Total surface area
total_area = sum(areas);

docs.title: Vertex Normals
docs.text:
Normal vector at each vertex (average of adjacent face normals):

normals = M.computeVertexNormals();  % [N × 3]

docs.title: Edge Lengths
docs.text:
edge_lengths = M.computeEdgeLengths();  % [E × 1]
mean_edge_length = mean(edge_lengths);

docs.title: The Cotangent Laplacian
docs.text:
The discrete Laplace-Beltrami operator on a triangle mesh is:

\[ L_{ij} = \begin{cases} \sum_{k \sim i} \cot \alpha_{ij} + \cot \beta_{ij} & \text{if } i = j \\ -(\cot \alpha_{ij} + \cot \beta_{ij}) & \text{if } i \sim j \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

where \(\alpha_{ij}\) and \(\beta_{ij}\) are the two angles opposite edge \((i,j)\).

% Compute Laplacian
L = M.cotLaplacian();  % Sparse matrix [N × N]

docs.title: Mass Matrix
docs.text:
The mass matrix \(M\) represents the area associated with each vertex:

\[ M_{ij} = \begin{cases} A_i & \text{if } i = j \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

where \(A_i\) is the area associated with vertex \(i\) (typically \(\frac{1}{3}\) of adjacent triangles).

% Compute mass matrix
M_mass = M.massMatrix();  % Diagonal matrix [N × N]

docs.title: 1. Triangle Mesh (Most Common)
docs.text:
Use case: Cortical surfaces, 3D shapes

M = bct.Manifold(V, F);

Requirements: - V: [N × 3] vertex positions - F: [M × 3] face indices

docs.title: 2. Graph (Abstract)
docs.text:
Use case: Connectivity analysis, abstract networks

% Create from adjacency matrix
W = sparse(adjacency_matrix);
M = bct.Manifold.fromGraph(W);

Requirements: - W: [N × N] symmetric sparse matrix (adjacency or weights)

docs.title: 3. Hybrid: Mesh with Custom Connectivity
docs.text:
Use case: Modify mesh topology while preserving geometry

M = bct.Manifold(V, F);
M.setCustomEdges(custom_edge_list);

docs.title: Subsampling
docs.text:
Reduce mesh resolution:

% Keep 50% of vertices
M_sub = M.subsample(0.5);

% Or specify target vertex count
M_sub = M.subsample('TargetVertices', 10000);

docs.title: Refinement
docs.text:
Increase mesh resolution:

% Subdivide each triangle into 4
M_refined = M.subdivide(1);

% Multiple subdivisions
M_fine = M.subdivide(2);  % 16 triangles per original

docs.title: Region Extraction
docs.text:
Extract a subregion:

% Define region by vertex indices
region_vertices = [100:500, 1000:1500];
M_region = M.extractRegion(region_vertices);

docs.title: Boundary Detection
docs.text:
% Find boundary edges (if mesh has holes)
boundary_edges = M.findBoundary();

% Check if mesh is closed
is_closed = M.isClosed();

docs.title: Triangle Quality
docs.text:
% Compute quality metrics
quality = M.triangleQuality();

% Metrics include:
% - Aspect ratio
% - Minimum angle
% - Area
% - Regularity

docs.title: Connectivity
docs.text:
% Vertex valence (number of neighbors)
valence = M.vertexValence();

% Most cortical meshes have valence ≈ 6
mean_valence = mean(valence);

docs.title: Curvature
docs.text:
% Mean curvature at each vertex
curvature = M.meanCurvature();

% Gaussian curvature
gaussian_curv = M.gaussianCurvature();

docs.title: FreeSurfer
docs.text:
% FreeSurfer stores surfaces as ?h.pial, ?h.white, etc.
% Use FreeSurfer MATLAB tools to load

addpath('/Applications/freesurfer/matlab');
[V, F] = read_surf('lh.pial');
M = bct.Manifold(V, F);

docs.title: BrainStorm
docs.text:
% Load BrainStorm cortex file
cortex = load('cortex_file.mat');
M = bct.Manifold(cortex.Vertices, cortex.Faces);

docs.title: GIFTI
docs.text:
% Requires GIFTI toolbox
g = gifti('surface.gii');
M = bct.Manifold(g.vertices, g.faces);

docs.title: Custom/Synthetic
docs.text:
% Create icosphere (for testing)
[V, F] = icosphere(4);  % 4 subdivisions
M = bct.Manifold(V, F);

docs.title: Basic Visualization
docs.text:
% Plot mesh
figure;
M.plot();

% With options
M.plot('FaceColor', [0.8 0.8 0.8], 'EdgeColor', 'none');

docs.title: Colored by Property
docs.text:
% Color by curvature
curvature = M.meanCurvature();
M.plot('CData', curvature);
colorbar;
title('Mean Curvature');

docs.title: Interactive Inspection
docs.text:
% Open in interactive viewer
bct.show.manifold(M);

docs.title: From Mesh to Full Analysis
docs.text:
% 1. Create manifold
M = bct.Manifold(V, F);

% 2. Create BCT object
B = bct.bct.fromManifold(M);

% 3. Compute eigenbasis
B.computeEigenbasis(100);

% 4. Now ready for signal processing
% B.Lambda is the spectral domain
% M is still accessible as B.Manifold

docs.title: Adding Temporal Dimension
docs.text:
% Add time axis to manifold
M.Time = bct.Time(200, 250);  % 200 samples at 250 Hz

% Now can create spatiotemporal signals
signal = bct.Signal(M, data_matrix, 'meg_data');  % [N × T]

docs.title: Geodesic Distance
docs.text:
Compute shortest path distances on the surface:

% Distance from vertex 100 to all others
source_vertex = 100;
distances = M.geodesicDistance(source_vertex);

% Pairwise distances (computationally expensive)
D = M.pairwiseGeodesicDistance([v1, v2, v3, v4]);

docs.title: Parallel Transport
docs.text:
Transport vectors along the surface:

% Transport vector from v1 to v2
vector_at_v1 = [1, 0, 0];  % Tangent vector
vector_at_v2 = M.parallelTransport(vector_at_v1, v1, v2);

docs.title: Heat Kernel
docs.text:
% Compute heat kernel signature
t = 1.0;  % Time parameter
hks = M.heatKernelSignature(t);

docs.title: ✅ Do’s
docs.text:
• Check mesh quality before analysis: 

    M.validateTopology();

  • Use appropriate resolution:

  • Too coarse: Miss features

  • Too fine: Slow computation

  • Normalize vertex positions if working with multiple subjects: 

    M.normalize();  % Center and scale

docs.title: ❌ Don’ts
docs.text:
• Don’t modify V or F directly without updating dependent properties
  • Don’t assume manifolds are closed (check with M.isClosed())
  • Don’t mix different coordinate systems (MNI, native, etc.) without transformation

docs.title: Issue: “Mesh has non-manifold vertices”
docs.text:
Cause: Vertex with non-disk neighborhood Fix: Clean mesh 

M_clean = M.cleanNonManifold();

docs.title: Issue: “Negative triangle areas”
docs.text:
Cause: Flipped face orientation Fix: Correct orientation 

M.flipFaces();

docs.title: Issue: “Disconnected components”
docs.text:
Cause: Mesh has separate pieces Fix: Extract largest component 

M_main = M.largestComponent();

docs.title: Concepts Overview
docs.text: This section introduces the mathematical and computational foundations of Bioctree. Understanding these concepts will help you design better analyses and interpret results correctly.

docs.title: The Big Picture
docs.text:
Bioctree combines three major areas:

  1. Spectral Geometry: Analysis of signals on manifolds using eigenmodes
  2. Graph Signal Processing: Extension of Fourier analysis to graphs
  3. Time-Frequency Analysis: Joint decomposition in space, time, and frequency

docs.title: Domains and Dual Spaces
docs.text:
At the heart of Bioctree is the concept of domain duality:

Domain ←→ Dual Domain
   ↕          ↕
Signal ←→ Transformed Signal

Every domain has a dual, and transforms move signals between them:

Domain Space Dual Dual Space Transform Manifold Vertices Lambda Eigenmodes Spectral Time Samples Omega Frequencies Fourier Graph Nodes Spectrum Graph Freq Graph Fourier

docs.title: The Fundamental Equation
docs.text:
For a signal \(f\) on manifold \(\mathcal{M}\), the spectral decomposition is:

\[ f = \sum_{i=1}^{N} \hat{f}_i \phi_i \]

Where: - \(\phi_i\) are eigenvectors of the Laplace-Beltrami operator - \(\hat{f}_i\) are spectral coefficients - \(N\) is the number of vertices

This is analogous to the Fourier series, but on arbitrary surfaces.

docs.title: 1. Manifolds
docs.text:
Learn about: - Surface representation (vertices and faces) - Mesh topology - Differential geometry on discrete meshes - The role of the cotangent Laplacian

Key takeaway: Manifolds are the geometric substrate where signals live.

docs.title: 2. Laplace-Beltrami Operator
docs.text:
Understand: - The continuous and discrete Laplace-Beltrami operators - Eigendecomposition and eigenmodes - Physical interpretation (heat diffusion) - Numerical computation via FEM

Key takeaway: The Laplace-Beltrami operator defines “frequency” on curved surfaces.

docs.title: 3. Graph Structure
docs.text:
Explore: - Graphs as discrete manifolds - Adjacency and Laplacian matrices - Graph Fourier transform - Connection to mesh processing

Key takeaway: Graphs generalize signal processing to arbitrary network topologies.

docs.title: 4. Joint Spectral Domain
docs.text:
Discover: - Tensor products of domains - Joint spectral-temporal analysis - 2D and higher-dimensional filters - Separable vs. non-separable kernels

Key takeaway: Joint domains enable multidimensional signal decomposition.

docs.title: 5. Wave Packets
docs.text:
Dive into: - Traveling waves on manifolds - Wave packet transforms - Localization in space and frequency - Applications to neural oscillations

Key takeaway: Wave packets detect coherent spatiotemporal patterns.

docs.title: 6. Dispersion
docs.text:
Master: - Dispersion relations \(\omega = \omega(\lambda)\) - Group velocity \(v_g = d\omega/d\lambda\) - Phase velocity \(v_p = \omega/\lambda\) - Detecting traveling waves

Key takeaway: Dispersion characterizes how waves propagate on surfaces.

docs.title: Notation Guide
docs.text: Throughout the documentation, we use consistent notation:

docs.title: Spatial/Geometric
docs.text:
• \(\mathcal{M}\): Manifold
  • \(V\): Vertex set, \(V = \{v_i\}_{i=1}^{N}\)
  • \(F\): Face set
  • \(N\): Number of vertices
  • \(\mathbf{x}_i\): Position of vertex \(i\) in \(\mathbb{R}^3\)

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
• \(\Delta\): Laplace-Beltrami operator
  • \(L\): Graph Laplacian matrix
  • \(M\): Mass matrix
  • \(W\): Adjacency/weight matrix

docs.title: Spectral
docs.text:
• \(\lambda_i\): \(i\)-th eigenvalue
  • \(\phi_i\) or \(\mathbf{u}_i\): \(i\)-th eigenvector
  • \(\hat{f}\): Spectral coefficients of signal \(f\)
  • \(\Lambda\): Spectral domain

docs.title: Temporal
docs.text:
• \(t\): Time
  • \(T\): Number of time points
  • \(f_s\): Sampling frequency
  • \(\omega\): Angular frequency
  • \(\Omega\): Frequency domain

docs.title: Signals & Filters
docs.text:
• \(f\): Signal on manifold
  • \(h\): Filter kernel
  • \(f \ast h\): Filtered signal (convolution)
  • \(\odot\): Element-wise multiplication

docs.title: Mathematical Prerequisites
docs.text: To fully understand Bioctree concepts, familiarity with the following is helpful:

docs.title: Essential
docs.text:
• Linear algebra (eigenvalues, eigenvectors, matrix operations)
  • Fourier analysis (basic transform theory)
  • Calculus (derivatives, integrals)

docs.title: Helpful
docs.text:
• Differential geometry (manifolds, curvature)
  • Numerical methods (finite elements, sparse solvers)
  • Signal processing (filtering, spectral analysis)

docs.title: Advanced (for deep understanding)
docs.text:
• Functional analysis (Hilbert spaces, operators)
  • Riemannian geometry (metrics, geodesics)
  • Harmonic analysis (generalized Fourier theory)

docs.title: Manifold ↔ Image
docs.text: Think of a cortical surface like a 2D image, but curved: - Image pixels → Manifold vertices - Image gradients → Tangent vectors on surface - Image smoothing → Heat diffusion on manifold

docs.title: Eigenmodes ↔ Musical Modes
docs.text: Like vibrating drum heads: - Low eigenmodes → Deep bass notes (smooth, global patterns) - High eigenmodes → High treble (sharp, local features) - Eigenvalues → Frequencies of vibration

docs.title: Spectral Filtering ↔ Audio EQ
docs.text: Just like adjusting bass/treble: - Low-pass filter → Remove details, keep smooth features - High-pass filter → Detect edges, remove smooth background - Band-pass filter → Focus on specific spatial scales

docs.title: Q: Why use eigenmodes instead of standard Fourier?
docs.text:
A: Standard Fourier assumes periodic, Euclidean domains (like a torus). Cortical surfaces are: - Non-periodic (finite extent) - Non-Euclidean (curved) - Irregular (non-uniform sampling)

Eigenmodes naturally adapt to the geometry.

docs.title: Q: How many eigenmodes do I need?
docs.text: A: It depends on: - Mesh resolution: Finer meshes need more modes - Signal complexity: Smooth signals need fewer modes - Rule of thumb: Start with \(K \approx N/100\) to \(N/10\)

docs.title: Q: What’s the difference between Manifold and Graph domains?
docs.text:
A: - Manifold: 2D surface embedded in 3D, has geometric properties (angles, areas) - Graph: Abstract network, only connectivity matters

Bioctree uses manifolds when geometry is important (e.g., cortical surfaces), graphs for pure connectivity.

docs.title: Q: Can I use bioctree for non-brain data?
docs.text: A: Absolutely! Any data on meshes or graphs: - 3D shape analysis - Social network dynamics - Sensor network data - Traffic flow on road networks - Climate data on Earth’s surface

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Wave packets are localized oscillatory patterns that propagate across manifolds. In neuroscience, they appear as traveling waves in cortical activity. Bioctree provides specialized tools for detecting and analyzing wave packets on cortical surfaces.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
A wave packet is a signal localized in both space and frequency:

\[ \psi(x, t) = A(x) e^{i(\mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{x} - \omega t)} \]

where: - \(A(x)\): Envelope (localization) - \(\mathbf{k}\): Wave vector (spatial frequency) - \(\omega\): Temporal frequency - \(\mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{x} - \omega t\): Phase

docs.title: On Manifolds
docs.text:
Replace Euclidean wave vector with eigenmode decomposition:

\[ \psi_i(t) = \sum_{k} a_k(t) \phi_k(x_i) \]

where \(a_k(t)\) are time-varying spectral coefficients.

docs.title: Dispersion Relation
docs.text:
Connects spatial and temporal frequencies:

\[ \omega = \omega(\lambda) \]

For cortical waves, common forms: - Diffusive: \(\omega \propto \lambda\) (linear) - Oscillatory: \(\omega \propto \sqrt{\lambda}\) (dispersive)

% Compute dispersion relation from data
B.computeDispersion();

% Access fitted relation
omega_lambda = B.Lambda.dispersion(lambdas);

% Visualize
B.Lambda.plotDispersion();

docs.title: Method 1: Template Matching
docs.text:
% Create wave packet filter
wp_filter = bct.Filter(joint_domain, 'wavepacket', ...
    'velocity', 0.5, ...        % Group velocity (m/s)
    'center_freq', 10, ...      % Central frequency (Hz)
    'bandwidth', 2, ...         % Frequency bandwidth (Hz)
    'spatial_sigma', 0.02);     % Spatial localization (m)

% Detect wave packets
wp_response = wp_filter.apply(signal);

% Find peaks (detected wave packets)
[peaks, locs] = findpeaks(wp_response.Data(:));

docs.title: Method 2: Time-Frequency Decomposition
docs.text:
% Continuous wavelet transform in joint domain
scales = logspace(log10(8), log10(30), 20);  % 8-30 Hz
cwt_coeffs = bct.transforms.cwtJoint(signal, scales, B);

% Identify wave packet regions
threshold = 3 * std(abs(cwt_coeffs(:)));
wp_mask = abs(cwt_coeffs) > threshold;

docs.title: Group Velocity
docs.text:
The speed of wave packet propagation:

\[ v_g = \frac{d\omega}{d\lambda} \] 
% Compute group velocity kernel
vg_kernel = B.Lambda.groupVelocity();

% Create velocity-selective filter
vg_filter = bct.Filter(joint, 'velocity', ...
    'target_velocity', 0.5, ...  % m/s
    'tolerance', 0.1);

% Extract waves at specific velocity
waves_05ms = vg_filter.apply(signal);

docs.title: 1. Envelope
docs.text:

% Visualize envelope

docs.title: 2. Instantaneous Phase
docs.text:
% Phase from analytic signal

% Phase velocity
phase_velocity = diff(unwrap(phase, [], 2), 1, 2) * fs / (2*pi);

docs.title: 3. Instantaneous Frequency
docs.text:
% Frequency from phase derivative
inst_freq = fs * diff(unwrap(phase, [], 2), 1, 2) / (2*pi);

% Average frequency per vertex

docs.title: Direction Detection
docs.text:
% Compute phase gradient (wave direction)
phase_grad = B.Manifold.computeGradient(phase(:, t));

% Direction vector at each vertex
wave_direction = phase_grad ./ vecnorm(phase_grad, 2, 2);

% Visualize as vector field

docs.title: Wave Speed Estimation
docs.text:
% Track phase front over time

phase_diff = phase(:, t2) - phase(:, t1);
time_diff = (t2 - t1) / fs;

% Speed = distance / time
distances = B.Manifold.geodesicDistance(source_vertex);
speed = distances ./ (phase_diff / (2*pi) * time_diff);

%% 1. Initialization

%% 2. Load Mesh

B = bct.bct.fromMesh(data.V, data.F);

fprintf('  Vertices: %d\n', B.Manifold.N);
fprintf('  Faces: %d\n', size(B.Manifold.F, 1));

%% 3. Compute Eigenbasis
fprintf('\nComputing eigenbasis...\n');
tic;
B.computeEigenbasis(100);
fprintf('  Completed in %.2f seconds\n', toc);

%% 4. Load Signal Data
% Example: MEG source-localized data
% In practice, load your data here
fprintf('\nCreating test signal...\n');
T = 200;
fs = 250;
B.Manifold.Time = bct.Time(T, fs);

% Simulate data (replace with real data)

sig = bct.Signal(B.Manifold, signal_data, 'test_signal');

%% 5. Spatial Filtering
fprintf('\nApplying spatial filter...\n');
spatial_filt = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'gaussian', ...
    'center', 0, 'sigma', 20);
sig_spatial = spatial_filt.apply(sig);

%% 6. Temporal Filtering
fprintf('Applying temporal filter (alpha band)...\n');
temporal_filt = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'bandpass', ...
    'low', 8, 'high', 12, 'taper', true);
sig_alpha = temporal_filt.apply(sig_spatial);

%% 7. Joint Filtering
fprintf('Applying joint filter...\n');
joint = bct.Joint(B.Lambda, B.Omega);
joint_filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'separable', ...
    'spatial', spatial_filt, ...
    'temporal', temporal_filt);
sig_joint = joint_filt.apply(sig);

%% 8. Visualization
fprintf('\nVisualizing results...\n');

figure('Position', [100, 100, 1400, 900]);

% Original
subplot(2,3,1);
bct.show.signal(B, sig, 'TimePoint', 100);
title('Original Signal');

% Spatially filtered
subplot(2,3,2);
bct.show.signal(B, sig_spatial, 'TimePoint', 100);
title('Spatial Filtering');

% Temporally filtered
subplot(2,3,3);
bct.show.signal(B, sig_alpha, 'TimePoint', 100);
title('Temporal Filtering (Alpha)');

% Joint filtered
subplot(2,3,4);
bct.show.signal(B, sig_joint, 'TimePoint', 100);
title('Joint Filtering');

% Time series at random vertex
vertex_idx = randi(B.Manifold.N);
time_vector = (0:T-1) / fs;

subplot(2,3,5);
plot(time_vector, sig.Data(vertex_idx, :), 'k', 'LineWidth', 0.5);
hold on;
plot(time_vector, sig_alpha.Data(vertex_idx, :), 'r', 'LineWidth', 1.5);
xlabel('Time (s)');
ylabel('Amplitude');
legend('Original', 'Alpha Filtered');
title(sprintf('Time Series (Vertex %d)', vertex_idx));
grid on;

% Eigenmode spectrum
subplot(2,3,6);
kernel = spatial_filt.evaluate();
plot(0:length(kernel)-1, kernel, 'LineWidth', 2);
xlabel('Eigenmode Index');
ylabel('Filter Gain');
title('Spatial Filter Kernel');
grid on;

%% 9. Save Results
fprintf('\nSaving results...\n');
bct_obj = bct.create('analysis_results');
bct_obj.write_raw(sig_joint.Data, fs);
bct_obj.write_graph(struct('V', data.V, 'F', data.F));

fprintf('✓ Analysis complete!\n');

docs.title: Multi-Band Decomposition

% Define frequency bands

bands.delta = [0.5, 4];

docs.text: Complete example demonstrating traveling wave detection in MEG data.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
% Initialize bioctree
bioctree_start;

% Load cortical mesh (fsaverage right hemisphere)
data = load('data/mesh/fsaverage_rh_pial.mat');
B = bct.bct.fromMesh(data.V, data.F);

% Compute eigenbasis
fprintf('Computing eigenbasis...\n');

docs.title: Simulate Traveling Wave Data
docs.text:
For demonstration, we’ll simulate a traveling wave:

% Parameters
N = B.Manifold.N;     % Number of vertices
T = 200;              % Time points
fs = 250;             % Sampling rate (Hz)
wave_freq = 10;       % Hz (alpha band)
wave_velocity = 0.5;  % m/s

% Add time dimension
B.Manifold.Time = bct.Time(T, fs);

% Create synthetic traveling wave
time = (0:T-1) / fs;
source_vertex = round(N / 4);  % Start from one location

% Compute distances from source
distances = B.Manifold.geodesicDistance(source_vertex);

% Create wave: phase = 2π(ft - x/v)
phase = 2 * pi * (wave_freq * time - distances / wave_velocity);
wave_signal = cos(phase);

% Add noise
noise_level = 0.5;
noisy_wave = wave_signal + noise_level * randn(size(wave_signal));

% Create signal object
sig = bct.Signal(B.Manifold, noisy_wave, 'simulated_wave');

docs.title: Step 1: Compute Dispersion Relation
docs.text:
fprintf('Computing dispersion relation...\n');
B.computeDispersion(sig);

% Visualize
figure('Position', [100, 100, 800, 400]);
B.Lambda.plotDispersion();
title('Empirical Dispersion Relation');

docs.title: Step 2: Create Wave Packet Filter
docs.text:
% Create joint domain
joint = bct.Joint(B.Lambda, B.Omega);

% Design wave packet filter
wp_filter = bct.Filter(joint, 'wavepacket', ...
    'velocity', 0.5, ...        % Target velocity
    'center_freq', 10, ...      % Alpha frequency
    'bandwidth', 2, ...         % ±2 Hz
    'spatial_sigma', 0.05);     % 5cm spatial extent

% Apply filter
fprintf('Detecting wave packets...\n');
wp_response = wp_filter.apply(sig);

docs.title: Step 3: Extract Wave Characteristics
docs.text:
% Compute analytic signal via Hilbert transform
analytic = hilbert(wp_response.Data, [], 2);

% Extract envelope
envelope = abs(analytic);

% Extract instantaneous phase
phase_instant = angle(analytic);

% Compute phase gradient (wave direction)
phase_grad = B.Manifold.computeGradient(phase_instant);

docs.title: Snapshot Comparison
docs.text:
figure('Position', [100, 100, 1400, 500]);

% Original signal
subplot(1,3,1);
bct.show.signal(B, sig, 'TimePoint', 100);
title('Original Signal (t=100)');
colorbar;

% Wave packet response
subplot(1,3,2);
bct.show.signal(B, wp_response, 'TimePoint', 100);
title('Wave Packet Response');
colorbar;

% Envelope
subplot(1,3,3);
bct.show.signal(B, envelope(:, 100));
title('Instantaneous Envelope');
colorbar;

docs.title: Phase Evolution
docs.text:
figure('Position', [100, 100, 1400, 500]);

time_points = [50, 100, 150];
for i = 1:length(time_points)
    subplot(1, 3, i);
    bct.show.phase(B, phase_instant(:, time_points(i)));
    title(sprintf('Phase at t=%d', time_points(i)));
end

docs.title: Wave Packet Movie
docs.text:
% Animate traveling wave detection
bct.show.wavepacket_movie(B, wp_response, ...
    'FrameRate', 20, ...
    'TimeRange', [50, 150]);

docs.title: Detect Wave Events
docs.text:
% Threshold envelope to find significant wave events
threshold = mean(envelope(:)) + 2 * std(envelope(:));
wave_events = envelope > threshold;

% Count events per time point
events_per_time = sum(wave_events, 1);

% Plot event detection
figure;
plot((0:T-1)/fs, events_per_time);
xlabel('Time (s)');
ylabel('Number of Vertices in Wave');
title('Wave Event Detection');
grid on;

docs.title: Estimate Wave Speed
docs.text:
% Track phase front over time
t1 = 80;
t2 = 120;
delta_t = (t2 - t1) / fs;

% Phase difference
delta_phase = phase_instant(:, t2) - phase_instant(:, t1);

% Unwrap phase
delta_phase_unwrap = mod(delta_phase + pi, 2*pi) - pi;

% Speed = distance / time for 2π phase change
wave_period = 1 / wave_freq;
speed_estimate = distances ./ (delta_phase_unwrap / (2*pi) * wave_period);

% Remove outliers
valid_speed = speed_estimate(abs(speed_estimate) < 2);  % < 2 m/s
mean_speed = mean(valid_speed);
std_speed = std(valid_speed);

fprintf('Estimated wave speed: %.2f ± %.2f m/s\n', mean_speed, std_speed);
fprintf('True wave speed: %.2f m/s\n', wave_velocity);

% Test multiple velocities
test_velocities = [0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0];  % m/s
responses = cell(length(test_velocities), 1);

for i = 1:length(test_velocities)
    filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'wavepacket', ...
        'velocity', test_velocities(i), ...
        'center_freq', 10, ...
        'bandwidth', 2);

    responses{i} = filt.apply(sig);
end

% Compare responses

for i = 1:length(test_velocities)
    subplot(2, 2, i);
    bct.show.signal(B, responses{i}, 'TimePoint', 100);
    title(sprintf('v = %.1f m/s', test_velocities(i)));
end

docs.title: Filters
docs.text: Filter design and application is central to signal processing in Bioctree. This section covers spatial, temporal, and joint-domain filtering approaches.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Bioctree provides a comprehensive filtering framework that operates on multiple domains:

  • Spatial domain (on the manifold)
  • Spectral domain (in eigenspace λ)
  • Temporal domain (along time axis)
  • Frequency domain (ω)
  • Joint domains (combinations of the above)

docs.title: Spatial Filters
docs.text:
Filters operating on the cortical mesh in the spatial or spectral (λ) domain.

Key concepts: - Low-pass, high-pass, and band-pass filters in eigenspace - Heat kernel and diffusion-based filters - Spatial localization properties - Chebyshev polynomial approximations

docs.title: Temporal Filters
docs.text:
Filters operating along the time axis or in frequency (ω) domain.

Key concepts: - Standard temporal filtering (FIR, IIR) - Frequency-domain filtering via FFT - Time-frequency trade-offs - Window functions and tapering

docs.title: Joint Filters (λ–ω)
docs.text:
Filters operating on tensor product spaces combining spatial and temporal/frequency domains.

Key concepts: - Spatiotemporal filtering - Time-varying spatial filters - Separable vs. non-separable kernels - Computational efficiency

docs.title: Wave Packet Filters
docs.text:
Specialized filters for wave packet analysis with joint time-frequency-space localization.

Key concepts: - Gabor-like filters on manifolds - Dispersion-aware filtering - Velocity-tuned kernels - Wave propagation analysis

docs.title: Design Workflow
docs.text:
1. Choose your domain: Spatial (Manifold/Lambda), Temporal (Time/Omega), or Joint
  2. Define kernel: Select fundamental kernel type (gaussian, heat, etc.)
  3. Set parameters: Cutoff frequencies, bandwidths, centers
  4. Apply filter: Use Filter.apply() on your signals
  5. Visualize results: Use bct.show functions to inspect filtered signals

docs.title: Joint Filters (λ–ω)
docs.text: Joint filters operate on the tensor product of spatial and temporal frequency domains, enabling simultaneous spatiotemporal-spectral decomposition.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Joint filtering combines spatial and temporal filtering in the Lambda × Omega domain, allowing detection of specific spatial patterns oscillating at specific frequencies.

docs.title: Creating Joint Filters
docs.text:
% Create joint domain
joint = bct.Joint(B.Lambda, B.Omega);

% Create filter on joint domain
joint_filt = bct.Filter(joint, kernel_type, parameters);

docs.title: 1. Separable Filters
docs.text:
Product of 1D filters:

% Spatial low-pass × Temporal alpha-band
spatial = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'lowpass', 'cutoff', 30);
temporal = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'bandpass', 'low', 8, 'high', 12);

joint_sep = bct.Filter(joint, 'separable', ...
    'spatial', spatial, 'temporal', temporal);

Efficient computation: Apply filters sequentially instead of 2D operation

docs.title: 2. Gaussian 2D
docs.text:
% 2D Gaussian centered at (mode=20, freq=10Hz)
joint_gauss = bct.Filter(joint, 'gaussian', ...
    'center', [20, 10], ...    % [spatial_mode, temporal_freq]
    'sigma', [5, 2]);          % [spatial_bw, temporal_bw]

docs.title: 3. Dispersion-Based
docs.text:
Uses empirical dispersion relation:

% Compute dispersion
B.computeDispersion(signal);

% Filter along dispersion curve
disp_filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'dispersion', ...
    'velocity', 0.5, ...       % Group velocity
    'bandwidth', 0.1);         % Velocity tolerance

docs.title: Alpha-Band Spatial Patterns
docs.text:
% Extract smooth spatial patterns in alpha band
alpha_smooth = bct.Filter(joint, 'gaussian', ...
    'center', [10, 10], ...    % Low spatial freq, 10 Hz
    'sigma', [5, 2]);

alpha_pattern = alpha_smooth.apply(signal);

docs.title: Multi-Band Spatial Decomposition
docs.text:
bands = {'delta', 'theta', 'alpha', 'beta'};
freq_ranges = [1, 4; 4, 8; 8, 12; 13, 30];
spatial_cutoff = 30;

for i = 1:length(bands)
    spatial_filt = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'lowpass', 'cutoff', spatial_cutoff);
    temporal_filt = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'bandpass', ...
        'low', freq_ranges(i,1), 'high', freq_ranges(i,2));

    joint_filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'separable', ...
        'spatial', spatial_filt, 'temporal', temporal_filt);

    results.(bands{i}) = joint_filt.apply(signal);
end

docs.title: Spatial Filters
docs.text: Spatial filters operate on the manifold or its spectral dual (Lambda domain) to process spatial structure of signals.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Spatial filtering in Bioctree modifies the spatial frequency content of signals on cortical surfaces or graphs, analogous to image filtering but adapted to curved geometries.

docs.title: Manifold Domain
docs.text:
Direct spatial operations (less common): 

filt = bct.Filter(B.Manifold, 'delta', 'x0', vertex_idx);

docs.title: Lambda Domain (Spectral)
docs.text:
Most spatial filtering happens here: 

filt = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'lowpass', 'cutoff', 30);

docs.title: 1. Low-Pass (Smoothing)
docs.text:
% Ideal low-pass
lp = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'lowpass', 'cutoff', 30);
smooth_signal = lp.apply(signal);

% Gaussian smoothing (preferred)
gauss = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'gaussian', 'center', 0, 'sigma', 15);
smooth_signal = gauss.apply(signal);

Effect: Removes fine spatial details, smooths across surface

Use cases: - Noise reduction - Multi-subject averaging - Visualization enhancement

docs.title: 2. High-Pass (Edge Detection)
docs.text:
% Ideal high-pass
hp = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'highpass', 'cutoff', 50);
edges = hp.apply(signal);

Effect: Retains sharp spatial changes, removes smooth background

Use cases: - Detect activation boundaries - Find spatial gradients - Highlight sulcal/gyral patterns

docs.title: 3. Band-Pass (Scale Selection)
docs.text:
% Select spatial scale
bp = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'bandpass', 'low', 20, 'high', 60);
mid_scale = bp.apply(signal);

% With smooth transitions
bp_smooth = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'bandpass', ...
    'low', 20, 'high', 60, 'taper', true);

Effect: Isolates specific spatial frequencies

Use cases: - Multi-scale decomposition - Texture analysis - Feature extraction at specific scales

docs.title: 4. Notch (Remove Specific Modes)
docs.text:
% Remove artifact in specific eigenmodes
notch = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'notch', 'center', 42, 'width', 2);
cleaned = notch.apply(signal);

docs.title: Kernel Functions
docs.text:
All fundamental kernels work on Lambda:

% Gaussian (smooth transition)
bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'gaussian', 'center', 25, 'sigma', 10);

% Box (ideal, ringing)
bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'box', 'center', 25, 'width', 20);

% Hamming window
bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'hamming', 'center', 25, 'width', 20);

% Custom kernel
custom_kernel = exp(-0.01 * B.Lambda.eigenvalues);
bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'custom', 'kernel', custom_kernel);

docs.title: Octave Bands
docs.text:
% Dyadic decomposition
num_octaves = 4;
base_freq = 10;

for oct = 1:num_octaves
    low = base_freq * 2^(oct-1);
    high = base_freq * 2^oct;

    filt = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'bandpass', 'low', low, 'high', high);
    scales{oct} = filt.apply(signal);
end

docs.title: Laplacian Pyramid
docs.text:
% Build pyramid
pyramid = bct.filters.buildPyramid(B, signal, 'Levels', 5);

% Reconstruct
reconstructed = bct.filters.reconstructPyramid(pyramid);

docs.title: Example 1: Noise Removal
docs.text:
% Add noise
noisy = signal;
noisy.Data = noisy.Data + 0.5 * randn(size(noisy.Data));

% Low-pass filter
denoised_filt = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'gaussian', 'center', 0, 'sigma', 20);
denoised = denoised_filt.apply(noisy);

% Compare
figure;
subplot(1,2,1); bct.show.signal(B, noisy); title('Noisy');
subplot(1,2,2); bct.show.signal(B, denoised); title('Denoised');

docs.title: Example 2: ROI Extraction
docs.text:
% Localize around vertex
roi_center = 5000;
roi_filter = bct.Filter(B.Manifold, 'delta', 'x0', roi_center);

% Transform to spectral
roi_spectral = B.Manifold.transform(roi_filter.evaluate(), B.Lambda);

% Create spatial window
spatial_window = B.Lambda.inverse(roi_spectral .* (B.Lambda.eigenvalues < 50));

docs.title: Example 3: Mesh-Adaptive Smoothing
docs.text:
% Smooth proportional to mesh resolution
edge_lengths = B.Manifold.computeEdgeLengths();
avg_edge = mean(edge_lengths);

% Sigma proportional to edge length
sigma = 10 * avg_edge;  % ~10 edge lengths

filt = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'gaussian', 'center', 0, 'sigma', sigma);

docs.title: Anisotropic Filtering
docs.text:
% Different smoothing in different directions
% (Requires directional decomposition)
tangent_filter = bct.Filter(B.Lambda, 'directional', ...
    'direction', direction_vector, ...
    'bandwidth', 20);

docs.title: Bilateral Filtering
docs.text:
% Edge-preserving smoothing
bilateral = bct.filters.bilateral(B, signal, ...
    'SpatialSigma', 15, ...
    'IntensitySigma', 0.5);

docs.title: Temporal Filters
docs.text: Temporal filters process the time-series aspect of spatiotemporal signals, operating in the Time or Omega (frequency) domains.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Temporal filtering in Bioctree follows standard time-series and frequency-domain filtering theory, integrated with the spatial domain framework.

docs.title: Time Domain
docs.text:
Direct temporal operations: 

filt = bct.Filter(B.Time, 'gaussian', 'center', 100, 'sigma', 10);

docs.title: Omega Domain (Frequency)
docs.text:
Most temporal filtering (like spatial → Lambda): 

filt = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'bandpass', 'low', 8, 'high', 12);

docs.title: 1. Band-Pass (Oscillation Extraction)
docs.text:
% Alpha band (8-12 Hz)
alpha_filt = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'bandpass', 'low', 8, 'high', 12);
alpha_signal = alpha_filt.apply(signal);

% Beta band (13-30 Hz)
beta_filt = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'bandpass', 'low', 13, 'high', 30);

% With smooth transitions (recommended)
alpha_smooth = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'bandpass', ...
    'low', 8, 'high', 12, 'taper', true);

Neurophysiological bands: - Delta: 0.5-4 Hz - Theta: 4-8 Hz - Alpha: 8-12 Hz - Beta: 13-30 Hz - Gamma: 30-100+ Hz

docs.title: 2. Low-Pass (Anti-Aliasing, Smoothing)
docs.text:
% Remove high frequencies
lp_filt = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'lowpass', 'cutoff', 40);
smooth_time = lp_filt.apply(signal);

docs.title: 3. High-Pass (DC Removal, Baseline)
docs.text:
% Remove slow drifts
hp_filt = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'highpass', 'cutoff', 1);
detrended = hp_filt.apply(signal);

docs.title: 4. Notch (Line Noise)
docs.text:
% Remove 50 Hz line noise (Europe)
notch_50 = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'notch', 'center', 50, 'width', 2);

% 60 Hz (North America)
notch_60 = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'notch', 'center', 60, 'width', 2);

% Apply
clean = notch_60.apply(signal);

docs.title: Example 1: Multi-Band Decomposition
docs.text:
% Define frequency bands
bands = struct();
bands.delta = [0.5, 4];
bands.theta = [4, 8];
bands.alpha = [8, 12];
bands.beta = [13, 30];
bands.gamma_low = [30, 60];

% Extract each band
decomposed = struct();
for name = fieldnames(bands)'
    band = bands.(name{1});
    filt = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'bandpass', ...
        'low', band(1), 'high', band(2), 'taper', true);
    decomposed.(name{1}) = filt.apply(signal);
end

docs.title: Example 2: Event-Related Filtering
docs.text:
% Filter around event frequency
event_freq = 2;  % Events at 2 Hz
event_filt = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'bandpass', ...
    'low', event_freq - 0.5, ...
    'high', event_freq + 0.5);

event_related = event_filt.apply(signal);

docs.title: Example 3: Downsampling with Anti-Aliasing
docs.text:
% Target sampling rate
fs_new = 125;  % Hz (from 250 Hz)

% Low-pass at Nyquist of new rate
lp = bct.Filter(B.Omega, 'lowpass', 'cutoff', fs_new/2);
filtered = lp.apply(signal);

% Downsample
downsample_factor = round(B.Manifold.Time.fs / fs_new);
downsampled = filtered.Data(:, 1:downsample_factor:end);

docs.title: Wave Packet Filters
docs.text: Specialized filters for detecting and extracting traveling wave packets on cortical surfaces.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Wave packet filters combine spatial localization, temporal frequency selectivity, and propagation velocity to detect coherent spatiotemporal patterns.

docs.title: Basic Wave Packet Filter
docs.text:
% Create wave packet filter
wp_filt = bct.Filter(joint, 'wavepacket', ...
    'velocity', 0.5, ...        % Group velocity (m/s)
    'center_freq', 10, ...      % Central frequency (Hz)
    'bandwidth', 2, ...         % Frequency bandwidth (Hz)
    'spatial_sigma', 0.02);     % Spatial extent (m)

% Apply to signal
wp_response = wp_filt.apply(signal);

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• velocity: Target group velocity (m/s or eigenmode/s)
  • center_freq: Dominant temporal frequency (Hz)
  • bandwidth: Frequency spread (Hz)
  • spatial_sigma: Spatial localization (meters or eigenmodes)

docs.title: Velocity-Selective Filtering
docs.text:
% Decompose by propagation speed
velocities = [0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.2];  % m/s

for i = 1:length(velocities)
    wp = bct.Filter(joint, 'wavepacket', ...
        'velocity', velocities(i), ...
        'center_freq', 10, ...
        'bandwidth', 2);

    components{i} = wp.apply(signal);
end

docs.title: Dispersion-Aware Wave Packets
docs.text:
% Use empirical dispersion relation
B.computeDispersion(signal);

% Filter respects dispersion
wp_disp = bct.Filter(joint, 'wavepacket', ...
    'dispersion', B.Lambda.dispersion, ...
    'velocity', 0.5, ...
    'center_freq', 10, ...
    'bandwidth', 2);

docs.title: Alpha Traveling Waves
docs.text:
% Detect alpha-band traveling waves
alpha_wp = bct.Filter(joint, 'wavepacket', ...
    'velocity', 0.3, ...        % Typical alpha velocity
    'center_freq', 10, ...      % Alpha peak
    'bandwidth', 2, ...
    'spatial_sigma', 0.05);     % ~5cm extent

alpha_waves = alpha_wp.apply(meg_signal);

% Visualize as movie
bct.show.wavepacket_movie(B, alpha_waves);

docs.title: Multi-Frequency Waves
docs.text:
% Detect waves at multiple frequencies
freqs = [6, 10, 15, 20];  % Hz

for i = 1:length(freqs)
    wp = bct.Filter(joint, 'wavepacket', ...
        'velocity', 0.5, ...
        'center_freq', freqs(i), ...
        'bandwidth', 2);

    waves{i} = wp.apply(signal);
end
